name: President Clubbs

tenures.source: The fed's own co-president, active from its earliest recruitment posts through its 25 May 1998 online-application announcement; billed on-air as 'President Clubbs' announcing the Championship Tournament bracket.

caption: One of the fed's own two co-presidents, billed on-air announcing the Championship Tournament that crowned its first champion.

name: Vice President Deeney

tenures.source: The fed's own co-president/vice-president, named in every sign-up form and appearing in-fiction backstage in the 27 April 1998 flash packet, discussing tournament and title plans with the wrestler Storm.

caption: The fed's own other co-president, appearing in-fiction backstage to discuss the fed's own upcoming tag title tournament.

name: Mark Williams

tenures.source: Signed among the fed's own earliest wrestlers; won the fed's own first Championship Tournament in a controversial triangle-match finish, then lost the belt at the fed's own first pay-per-view.

caption: A self-proclaimed 'Greatest of All Time' who won the fed's first Championship Tournament in a finish the broadcast itself leaves ambiguous, thanks to a lookalike twin brother.

name: Chris Williams

tenures.source: Introduced at the Championship Triangle Match as Mark Williams's identical twin brother and the newest member of The Great Ones; competed at the TV Title Battle Royal (eliminated by Bill Vaughn) and factored into the fed's own first pay-per-view main event.

caption: Mark Williams's identical twin brother, introduced mid-match at the Championship Triangle Match and central to the broadcast's own unresolved question of who actually won it.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is held under another promotion; nothing in the wing's own record links the two beyond a common, unremarkable wrestling gimmick name.

name: "Critical" Bill Vaughn

tenures.source: Signed among the fed's own earliest wrestlers; reached the tournament final, then won the fed's own Heavyweight Championship at its first pay-per-view.

caption: A brawler who earned his nickname sending opponents to 'critical condition,' and the fed's own second Heavyweight Champion.

name: Justin Credible

tenures.source: Signed among the fed's own earliest wrestlers, allied with Mark Williams as 'The Great Ones'; competed through the tournament and the TV Title Battle Royal.

caption: A technical wrestler managed by Heather, allied with Mark Williams as 'The Great Ones.'

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is held under another promotion; nothing in the wing's own record links the two beyond a common, unremarkable wrestling gimmick name.

name: "Hollywood" Steve Shine

tenures.source: Signed among the fed's own earliest wrestlers, managed by Krystal Powers; won the TV Championship twice, the second time by hiding under the ring for an entire battle royal.

caption: A vain heel managed by Krystal Powers who twice won the fed's Television Championship, once by ambushing the battle royal's actual winner after hiding under the ring the whole match.

name: Death

tenures.source: Signed among the fed's own earliest wrestlers; a recurring rival of the stable HC-2000, eliminating its leader Spider at the TV Title Battle Royal after a mystery ally attacked Spider from the rafters at the fed's own Championship Triangle Match.

caption: A masked monster whose ongoing feud with the stable HC-2000 ran through the fed's whole documented run.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is held under another promotion; nothing in the wing's own record links the two beyond a common, unremarkable wrestling gimmick name.

name: Spider

tenures.source: Signed among the fed's own earliest wrestlers; leader of the stable HC-2000, reached the tournament final before being eliminated by countout.

caption: The masked leader of the stable HC-2000, eliminated in the fed's own Championship Triangle Match by countout during his own rivals' rafters ambush.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is held under another promotion; nothing in the wing's own record links the two beyond a common, unremarkable wrestling gimmick name.

name: Sha Dog

tenures.source: A founding member of the stable HC-2000, eliminated in the first round of the Championship Tournament and again early at the TV Title Battle Royal.

caption: A founding member of the stable HC-2000.

name: James The Hitman

tenures.source: A founding member of the stable HC-2000; his first-round Championship Tournament match against Death ended in a disqualification when the rest of HC-2000 interfered.

caption: A founding member of the stable HC-2000, master of a finishing choke slam he calls the Choke Anger.

name: John McKenzie

tenures.source: A newcomer from Melbourne, Australia who won the TV Title Battle Royal in his debut match, lost it minutes later to a wrestler who had hidden under the ring, then regained it at the fed's own first pay-per-view.

caption: An Australian brawler who won the vacant Television Championship in his own debut match, only to lose it minutes later to a wrestler who had spent the entire battle royal hiding under the ring.

name: Freight

tenures.source: One half of the tag team Rail Road Express, managed by Sammy; won the fed's own first Tag Team Championship at its first pay-per-view and joined the stable Revolution Zero the same night.

caption: One half of the tag team Rail Road Express, and the fed's own first Tag Team Champion alongside his partner Diesel.

name: Diesel

tenures.source: One half of the tag team Rail Road Express, managed by Sammy; won the fed's own first Tag Team Championship at its first pay-per-view and joined the stable Revolution Zero the same night.

caption: One half of the tag team Rail Road Express, and the fed's own first Tag Team Champion alongside his partner Freight.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is held under another promotion; nothing in the wing's own record links the two beyond a common, unremarkable wrestling gimmick name.

name: Mars

tenures.source: One half of the tag team The Gods, managed by Hades; lost the fed's own first Tag Team Championship match to Rail Road Express at the fed's first pay-per-view.

caption: One half of the tag team The Gods, defeated for the fed's inaugural Tag Team Championship.

identity.note: A different persona of the same name is held under another promotion; nothing in the wing's own record links the two beyond a common, unremarkable wrestling gimmick name.

name: Apollo

tenures.source: One half of the tag team The Gods, managed by Hades; lost the fed's own first Tag Team Championship match to Rail Road Express at the fed's first pay-per-view.

caption: One half of the tag team The Gods, defeated for the fed's inaugural Tag Team Championship.
